Shrinkage plot of posterior means against estimates

Source: R/plot-shrinkage.R
plot_shrinkage.Rd

The shrinkage of a site is the difference between its estimate and the posterior mean of its effect. plot_shrinkage() shows it by plotting the posterior means against the estimates. An imprecise estimate far from the values supported by the estimated distribution of effects is shrunk strongly toward them, while a precise estimate is hardly changed.

Usage

plot_shrinkage(
  x,
  style = c("scatter", "arrows"),
  color_by = c("sigma", "truth", "none"),
  normal = FALSE,
  highlight = NULL,
  truth = NULL,
  scale = 1,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A bef_fit object created by bayes_efron_fit().

style

One of "scatter" (the default) for a scatterplot of posterior means against estimates, or "arrows" for an arrow from the estimate to the posterior mean of each site.

color_by

Variable shown by the color of a site: "sigma" (the default) for the standard error, "truth" for the true effect specified in truth, or "none". If truth is specified and color_by is not, the color shows the true effects.

normal

If TRUE, a panel is added for the normal random-effects model fitted to the same estimates by restricted maximum likelihood. Can also be a numeric vector c(mean = , sd = ), which adds a panel for the normal model with that mean and standard deviation.

highlight

Sites to show in a different color and to label, specified as a numeric vector of positions in the data or a character vector of site labels. If NULL (the default), no site is highlighted.

truth

An optional numeric vector with the true effect of every site, for simulated data.

scale

Positive number by which the effects are multiplied in the plot, e.g., scale = 100 to show differences in proportions as percentage points.

...

These dots are for future extensions and must be empty.

Value

A ggplot object.

Details

In the scatterplot (style = "scatter"), each site is a point with its estimate on the horizontal axis and its posterior mean on the vertical axis. The two axes have the same scale, and the color of a point shows the standard error of its estimate. A point on the dashed diagonal has not been moved, and the vertical distance of a point from the diagonal is the shrinkage of the site.

In the arrow plot (style = "arrows"), each site is an arrow from its estimate to its posterior mean, plotted at the height of its standard error, so color is not needed to show the standard error. Sites are labeled if there are 30 or fewer. If there are more than 100 sites, the arrows have no heads and a point marks the posterior mean.

If truth is specified, the color shows the true effects unless color_by is set, and style = "arrows" also marks them with crosses if there are at most 100 sites. In both styles, the points and arrows are semi-transparent if there are more than 100 sites, so that regions where they overlap appear darker.

The panel added by normal shows the same plot for a normal random-effects model: the mean of each effect given its estimate. These are plug-in means, i.e., the mean and the standard deviation of the model are fixed at their estimates. The normal model shrinks every estimate toward a single mean, by a fraction that depends only on the standard error. This package's model instead shrinks an estimate toward the values supported by \(g\).

See also

site_summary(), plot_sites(), vignette("plots")

Examples

# The callback gaps in percentage points: imprecise estimates far from
# the bulk are shrunk the most.
plot_shrinkage(krw_fit, scale = 100)


# The arrows style, for 19 studies.
plot_shrinkage(raudenbush_fit, style = "arrows")


# Simulated sites with two groups of true effects, with a panel for the
# normal model.
plot_shrinkage(twin_towers_fit, normal = TRUE, truth = twin_towers$theta_true)
